hypothesis: If the claim holds, GBIF has essentially no native (non-introduced) occurrence records of Amphibia (frogs, toads, newts) on genuinely oceanic islands, though introduced populations may be recorded there.
pass_criterion: From a list of at least 20 oceanic islands or archipelagos fixed in advance (for example Hawaii, Galapagos, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Mauritius, Reunion, Bermuda, Society Islands, Marquesas, Samoa, Tonga, Cook Islands), at least 95% have zero native amphibian species after excluding records marked INTRODUCED or INVASIVE and records with coordinate-error flags.
fail_criterion: More than 10% of the pre-listed oceanic islands or archipelagos have at least one native amphibian species supported by verified, non-introduced records. A result between 5% and 10% is inconclusive.
interpretation: 'Batrachians' maps to the class Amphibia (GBIF taxon key 131), including Anura and Caudata, plus caecilians as a modern addition. 'Oceanic islands' means volcanic or coral islands never joined to a continent, which excludes continental fragments such as Madagascar, the granitic Seychelles and New Zealand. 'Naturally absent' maps to no records with establishmentMeans native, or unspecified but not introduced, once errors are removed. 'Introduced frogs thrive' maps to records with establishmentMeans INTRODUCED. The sea-water mortality mechanism cannot be tested with this dataset, so only the distributional generalization is tested.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (Amphibia, taxon key 131)
dataset.why_it_fits: The GBIF occurrence API and downloads provide taxonKey, species, country, islandGroup, island, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord, coordinates and geospatial issue flags. These allow native versus introduced amphibian records to be counted on each pre-listed oceanic island, excluding flagged errors.
